title: Quantum-Dot Sensitized Solar Cells Employing Hierarchical Cu2S Microspheres Wrapped by Reduced Graphene Oxide Nanosheets as Effective Counter Electrodes

nodes.label: QDSSCs need a cheap counter electrode that reduces polysulfide fast; Pt is expensive and is poisoned by the polysulfide electrolyte
Wrapping hierarchical Cu2S microspheres in reduced graphene oxide should add conductive paths and accessible catalytic sites and so raise the cell efficiency
Hierarchical Cu2S microspheres built from nanoflakes as the counter-electrode catalyst
Add graphene oxide to the same solvothermal bath so that RGO nanosheets form and wrap the microspheres in one step
GO ethanol solution volume 0, 5, 10 and 20 mL, giving Cu2S and RGO-Cu2S-1/2/3 (26.8, 41.4, 55.3 wt% RGO); Pt as the reference electrode
One-step solvothermal reaction of 0.05 M CuCl, 0.1 M thiourea and 0.3 g PVP with GO in ethanol at 150 C for 12 h
Calcination of the product at 350 C in Ar
Hierarchical microspheres built from nanoflakes; with GO the flakes become much finer and more numerous, giving a flower-like sphere
RGO nanosheets partially and irregularly wrap the microspheres; coverage grows with GO until at 20 mL the spheres are buried in crumpled sheets
The RGO composite is more porous: higher adsorbed volume at every relative pressure and a mesoporous, interparticle pore network (20.11 vs 14.59 m2/g)
GO is reduced during the solvothermal step: the oxygen-containing groups are removed and a graphitic RGO network remains
The composite electrode is a far better polysulfide-reduction catalyst than Pt: about 100x the reduction peak current and the highest exchange current density

attrs.quantity: reduction peak current density, exchange current density

nodes.label: Charge-transfer resistance at the electrode/electrolyte interface falls to about 3.4 ohm for RGO-Cu2S-2, roughly half that of Cu2S and far below Pt
The RGO sheets bridge the microspheres to the FTO and open a mesoporous surface, so electrons reach more accessible catalytic sites
A CdS/CdSe QDSSC with the RGO-Cu2S-2 counter electrode reaches 3.85% efficiency (Voc 0.556 V, Jsc 15.85 mA/cm2, FF 0.44) under AM 1.5G

attrs.condition: AM 1.5G, 0.20 cm2 active area, polysulfide electrolyte

nodes.label: Past 10 mL GO the extra RGO covers the Cu2S surface and blocks electrolyte access, so efficiency falls back to 2.99% for RGO-Cu2S-3
10 mL GO, about 41 wt% RGO, is the optimum wrapping: enough conductive network without burying the catalyst
One-step solvothermal RGO wrapping turns hierarchical Cu2S microspheres into a Pt-free counter electrode that outperforms both Pt and bare Cu2S
The nanoflakes are single-crystal monoclinic Cu2S (JCPDS 33-0490); no second phase appears with RGO
3.85% against 3.39% for pristine Cu2S and 2.14% for Pt under the same photoanode and electrolyte
Without GO the spheres carry coarse blade-like flakes; with GO the flakes become fine, dense and evenly packed over the sphere surface

nodes.label: IPCE of the RGO-Cu2S cell is highest across 330-620 nm, peaking near 95% at 345 nm against about 87% for Cu2S and 65% for Pt; all share a 640 nm onset
Pt counter electrodes are poisoned in polysulfide electrolyte, and Cu2S is the standard alternative for QDSSCs
JCPDS card 33-0490 for monoclinic Cu2S
Band assignments: 3411 cm-1 O-H, 1726 cm-1 C=O, 1583 vs 1604 cm-1 G band of RGO vs GO; Cu LMM at 569.6 eV is Cu(I)
For a QDSSC counter electrode the cathodic peak current of the voltammogram is the measure of catalytic ability for Sx2- reduction
Equivalent circuit Rs + Rct1/CPE1 + Rct2/CPE2, in which Rct2 is the electrode/electrolyte charge-transfer resistance

notes: Two parallel structure branches meet at the device: morphology/porosity -> catalytic activity, and GO reduction -> conductivity -> charge-transfer resistance. The RGO-Cu2S-3 downturn is carried by MEC/tradeoff with a counteracts edge into the PRF node. Lost: TGA RGO fractions, EDS, XPS (F4 not opened), the supplementary stability cycling and UV-vis of the photoanode, and Table 1, which holds the PCE values of RGO-Cu2S-1 and -3 (only the best CE is plotted in F5). Image findings: the claimed monotonic growth of the microspheres from 2 to 5 um is not visible against the panels' own scale bars (q3, image_support contradicts); the reduction-peak difference between Cu2S and RGO-Cu2S-2 is within the line width (q15); the F2d caption calls the SAED pattern that of the microsphere while the text calls it that of the nanoflake; the F3b inset pore-size distributions both peak near 20 nm and do not show the tabulated 6.61 vs 11.33 nm averages. Panel-section problems: the F1d and F5b crops are labelled 'letter p'/'letter q (OCR DISAGREES)' - both are really (d) and (b); the F1c cue line reads 'scale bar 500mm' for a 500 nm bar; the F1b definition string carries the caption typo 'RGO-Cu2S-7' for RGO-Cu2S-1.

changes: q3: image_note corrected - against its own 5 um bar the 10 mL panel gives spheres of roughly 2-3 um, not 3 um; the contradiction of the quoted 2->5 um growth is if anything stronger than the node claimed

panel_checks.note: both crops carry their own scale bars (2 um and 5 um) and their magnified single-sphere insets; the spheres in (c) are not larger than those in (a), so image_support = contradicts is right
the Raman panel prints 1335 and 1583 on the RGO-Cu2S trace, 1335 and 1604 on the GO trace, and 2705, 2971, 3136 on the second-order region - exactly the node's numbers

the Nyquist panel reaches Z' about 2600 ohm for Pt and its inset gives the second semicircle as about 7.5-15 ohm for Cu2S against about 7.5-11 ohm for RGO-Cu2S; the Rs + Rct1/CPE1 + Rct2/CPE2 circuit is drawn inside the panel

review.audit_summary: 2 audits (q3 sphere size contradicting the text, q15 unresolved CV peak difference). Both are stated as what the panel does and does not resolve rather than as errors, and both bear on spine claims (b8 and b12). Under the audit budget of 5 there was room for more, but no further figure finding changed spine support.
